analysis:
Both changed files are test-only: provider-swift/Tests/ClusterInstalledSessionChecks/InstalledBatchLanesCheck.swift and InstalledFixture.swift. They are not shipped runtime code. They introduce no new attack surface and weaken no control in the threat model.

InstalledFixture.swift (head lines 25, 61, 80) adds an optional prefillSchedule parameter. When it is set, the fabricated capability advertises all ClusterPrefillSchedule cases and the setup JSON carries prefillSchedule. When it is not set, only [.serial] is advertised.

InstalledBatchLanesCheck.swift (head lines 204-220) adds assertions on the Gemma4 layer-stage pipeline:
- A serial-prefill plan defaults to DistributedInstalledPlan.gemma4PipelineBatchLanes, and lanesRetireAlone is true.
- That default reaches the native worker environment through the actual sanitized owner child.
- A saved oneChunkLookahead plan stays at 1 lane, and lanesRetireAlone is false.

The pre-existing sanitization checks are unchanged. These cover the fixed owner environment, rejection of DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES and unrelated variables, bounds on lane counts, and removal of the contiguous-KV switch. The new tests add coverage and do not relax any of them.

The production change implied by these tests (a Gemma default of four lanes in DistributedInstalledPlan, and the lookahead gating) is not in the supplied units. Its correctness is unverified. Reviewers of the production source should confirm three points:
- The default lane count is applied identically in provider admission, in the owner lease and in the native worker.
- Per-request memory and quota bounds still hold at four lanes.
- Cancellation isolation (lanesRetireAlone) is consistent between provider and owner.

The fixture's fixtureArtifacts stand-in for pair-serving grants is explicitly check-build only and is unchanged here.

No finding is raised.
